Consult Summary:
- 53-year-old male presents with a 1-week history of painless swelling of the left elbow, suspected to be olecranon bursitis, managed with NSAIDs and scheduled blood tests for further evaluation.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Painless swelling over left elbow for approximately 1 week.
- Noticed incidentally in the shower; described as feeling a bit "weird," slightly warm, with a sense of fluid beneath the skin.
- No pain at baseline; no significant restriction in movement; able to move elbow normally.
- Swelling is slightly warm compared to adjacent skin; some discomfort or “weird” feeling when pressing near the swelling.
- Denies history of trauma, injury, or recent physical exertion.
- No prior similar episodes.
- Denies systemic symptoms (no mention of fever, malaise, or other joint involvement).
- No history or current presence of skin conditions such as eczema; reports dryness of skin only at elbow tip.
- Review of systems otherwise unremarkable.

Past Medical History:
- Osteoarthritis, diagnosed by GP a few years ago; occasional joint pain noted.
- No other chronic illnesses reported.
- No documented assessment or complications related to osteoarthritis.

Medications:
- No regular medications.
- Advised to take ibuprofen 400 mg twice daily after food (NSAID); instructed to stop if heartburn occurs.
- Allergic to peanuts.
- No known drug allergies.

Social History:
- Occupation: Desk-based, sedentary work; not physically demanding.
- Regular runner (2–3 times per week); considers self generally healthy, mobile, and active.
- No mention of smoking, alcohol, or recreational drug use.
- No relevant financial or lifestyle stressors reported.

Family History:
- No known family history of rheumatological diseases (e.g., rheumatoid arthritis, lupus); not aware of significant family history.

Physical Examination:
- Limited physical exam via video:
  - Visible swelling over the left elbow.
  - Slightly warm to touch compared to adjacent skin.
  - Full range of movement; no limitation reported.
  - Skin at tip of elbow appears dry; no other dermatosis reported or observed.
  - No pronounced tenderness at the tip of the elbow; some abnormal sensation adjacent to swelling.
  - No comment on redness, fluctuation, systemic signs, or vital signs.

Investigations:
- Plan for blood tests: inflammatory markers, infection markers, rheumatological screen, uric acid (gout), and other relevant labs.
- No prior investigations documented; pending blood work as above.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Left elbow swelling (likely bursitis)
  - Suspected olecranon bursitis; no features suggestive of septic arthritis.
  - Prescribed ibuprofen 400 mg BID after food for inflammation, with advice to discontinue if GI symptoms occur.
  - Arranged blood tests for inflammatory markers, infection, rheumatologic antibodies, and gout screen.
  - Arrange follow-up to review clinical course and blood test results.
  - Patient advised to escalate care if elbow becomes very red, more painful, or if redness spreads (to rule out evolving infection/sepsis).
- Issue 2: Osteoarthritis
  - Previous GP diagnosis; occasional joint pains.
  - No specific current intervention required beyond standard advice.
- General Plan
  - Blood test forms to be mailed to patient; instructions included.
  - Results expected in 5–6 days after test performed.
  - Follow-up to be arranged post-investigation, with flexibility for virtual or in-person review.

Quality checks (document_quality):
●	Missing elements: No detailed medication reconciliation (other than NSAID and mention of none regular), family history limited; no vital signs; no detailed exam beyond video inspection.
●	No internal conflicts noted.
●	Transcript quality: Clear and comprehensive; minor conversational filler, but clinical details well elicited. No notable inaudible segments.
